abstracts.abstract: This paper presents a novel stochastic geometry framework for analyzing ultra-dense cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) networks operating in millimeter-wave (mmWave) bands. Unlike conventional蜂窝系统 analysis that relies on Wyner-type models or grid-based deployments, we develop a continuum percolation theory approach to characterize the asymptotic behavior of interference and spectral efficiency. By modeling access points as a Poisson point process with tunable clustering, we derive closed-form expressions for the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio distribution and outage probability under spatially correlated mmWave channels. The proposed framework accounts for directional beamforming, blockage effects, and hardware impairments that are critical in practical系统设计. Our analysis reveals a fundamental phase transition phenomenon: below a critical node density, network performance is interference-limited, while beyond this threshold, beamforming gains dominate. This finding overturns the conventional wisdom that denser deployments always improve performance in interference-limited systems. Simulation results validate the theoretical derivations and demonstrate that the optimal access point density depends on beamforming capability and blockage intensity. This work establishes a new paradigm for analyzing future 6G cell-free architectures, providing rigorous theoretical foundations for resource allocation optimization.

This paper develops an enhanced channel estimation framework for massive MIMO systems operating over doubly-selective channels, addressing the fundamental challenge of pilot contamination in time-varying environments. Existing compressive sensing approaches suffer from high computational complexity or inadequate modeling of temporal correlation. We propose a novel multi-block sparse Bayesian learning algorithm that jointly exploits the structured sparsity in the delay-Doppler domain and the temporal evolution of channel paths. By introducing a dynamic Gaussian mixture prior that captures path birth-death dynamics, the proposed method significantly reduces the required pilot overhead while maintaining estimation accuracy. Theoretical analysis establishes that the mean squared error decays as O(1/N) with the number of antennas N, representing a square-root improvement over existing methods under mobility. Furthermore, we derive the minimum pilot sequence length for reliable channel tracking, which is shown to scale logarithmically with the number of antennas. Extensive numerical results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves near-optimal performance with 40% fewer pilots compared to state-of-the-art methods in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing systems. This work provides rigorous theoretical guarantees for practical massive MIMO deployment in high-speed scenarios.

This paper introduces a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-empowered secure communication architecture for future wireless networks, marking a paradigm shift from conventional physical layer security approaches. Traditional加密方案 incur significant overhead and computational burden, particularly in资源受限的ad hoc networks. The proposed system leverages an RIS with a novel hybrid beamforming architecture that simultaneously performs information beamforming toward legitimate users and artificial noise generation toward potential eavesdroppers. We design a deep reinforcement learning framework to optimize the RIS phase shifts and transmit covariance matrices in real-time, adapting to dynamic wireless propagation environments. The architecture incorporates an on-surface signal processing unit that enables distributed optimization without centralized coordination, addressing scalability concerns in大规模部署. Field trials in an indoor vehicular network testbed at 28 GHz demonstrate that the proposed system achieves a 15 dB security margin improvement over conventional approaches while maintaining communication reliability. The system architecture supports seamless integration with existing cellular systems and sensor networks, providing backward compatibility. This work establishes a practical pathway for deploying intelligent reflecting surfaces in real-world security-critical communication scenarios.

This paper presents an enhanced spectrum sensing protocol for cognitive radio networks that significantly improves detection reliability in low signal-to-noise ratio environments. Existing energy detection methods face fundamental limitations including vulnerability to noise uncertainty and inability to distinguish primary user signals from similar modulation formats. We propose a novel hybrid sensing framework that combines feature-assisted detection with adaptive compressive sampling. The protocol employs a dynamic threshold mechanism that adjusts sensing parameters based on real-time channel quality assessment and interference temperature. A key innovation is the incorporation of ambient backscatter communication principles, enabling passive sensing without dedicated hardware. We develop a cross-layer design that jointly optimizes sensing duration, transmission power, and routing in cognitive ad hoc networks. Implementation on software-defined radio platforms demonstrates successful detection of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing signals at -25 dB SNR with sensing time reduced by 60%. The proposed system achieves a goodput improvement of 35% compared to existing protocols while ensuring strict interference protection for primary users. Practical considerations including hardware constraints and energy efficiency are thoroughly addressed, making the solution suitable for deployment in energy-constrained sensor networks.
